title: Disparate Impact in Synthetic Data Generation
abstract: arXiv:2606.13105v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We revisit the fairness notion of disparate impact for synthetic data generation (SDG), that assesses whether the utility of generated records is the same across sensitive groups. Our approach departs from existing work on fair SDG, that address the problem of correcting for undue biases in the observed distribution, hence redefining SDG as learning a distribution that is not that of the real data. By contrast, non-disparate impact is notably achieved when the synthetic and real distributions are the same. We expose reasons why SDG may fail to reach that solution and discuss why approximation and estimation errors occur and can be disparate across groups. We notably look into the expressive power of SDG methods relative to distribution complexity, sampling errors due to group proportions, and estimation errors induced by differential privacy mechanisms. translated_title: 合成数据生成中的差别影响
translated_abstract: 我们重新审视了合成数据生成（SDG）中“差别影响”这一公平性概念，该概念用于评估生成的记录在不同敏感群体之间是否具有相同的效用。我们的方法有别于现有的公平SDG研究——后者致力于纠正观测分布中的不当偏差，从而将SDG重新定义为学习一个不同于真实数据的分布。相比之下，当合成分布与真实分布相同时，即可实现无差别影响。我们揭示了SDG可能无法达到该目标的原因，并讨论了近似误差和估计误差为何会出现，以及为何这些误差在不同群体间可能存在差异。我们特别研究了SDG方法相对于分布复杂度的表达能力、由群体比例导致的采样误差，以及由差分隐私机制引入的估计误差。我们在人工数据和真实世界数据上展示了差别影响的案例。
tldr: 本文重新审视了合成数据生成中的差别影响公平性问题，指出当合成分布与真实分布一致时即可实现无差别影响，并分析了模型表达能力、群体比例导致的采样误差以及差分隐私机制如何在不同群体间造成差异化误差。
en_tdlr: This paper revisits the fairness notion of disparate impact in synthetic data generation, showing that non-disparate impact is achieved when synthetic and real distributions coincide, and analyzes how model expressive power, group-proportion sampling errors, and differential privacy mechanisms can produce disparate errors across sensitive groups.
